name: Process Street
summary: Recurring work as trackable checklists and SOPs, with approvals and conditional logic.
best_for: operations-driven teams that run recurring, checklist-based processes and want them tracked and auditable
skip_if: you just need to write down a few SOPs — a doc or a cheaper tool captures them without the platform cost
honest_knock: Pricing is opaque and jumps steeply from Startup to Pro, with seat minimums that push the real cost above the headline per-member rate — you'll need a sales call to price it. Best once recurring checklists are core to how you operate.

plans.name: Startup

plans.name: Pro

pricing.plans_source: summarised from pricing.notes; every plan name and amount appears verbatim in those notes
pricing.notes: Process Street publishes no prices. Re-verified 2026-08-17, 2026-09-30 and 2026-10-06: every tier on their pricing page, Startup included, shows Contact sales rather than a figure, and our monthly captures from July and August 2026 are byte-for-byte identical and contain no amount. What the page does publish are the limits. Startup is capped at 5 users and 10 guests, with 5,000 Data Set records, 10 automation apps, 100 automation actions a month and a public API limited to 50 calls a month. The page describes it as a simplified Pro plan for startups. Pro comes with a 14-day free trial that needs no credit card. Figures quoted elsewhere — roughly $100 a month for Startup, the $1,500 range for Pro, per-member rates around $12.50 to $15 — do not come from Process Street and we could not verify any of them. The FAQ on the same page adds one lever the plan cards do not show: discounts for registered non-profits, arranged through sales.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 23 October 2026 during the Pro trial, without a card and without integrations: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. We had the AI build a purchase-approval workflow (purchase ID and amount, a budget and a supplier check, manager approval, at most six steps), ran it twice with known amounts, completed one run with approval, left the other open, and exported the Reports views.
findings: Generate with AI (a name plus instructions) produced the workflow in about 30 seconds: exactly the six steps we asked for, with full task texts and checklists, 35 form fields, 6 dynamic due dates, 1 approval step and 0 stop tasks. Starting a run added a seventh task, 'Role assignments', with four roles the AI invented, such as procurement analyst and finance analyst. That is a lot of fields for a simple approval.

Tasks could be ticked off while most of the 35 fields were still empty: no field was required. Values we entered were saved straight away, and completing a task gave the next one a due date automatically.

The approval step listed every earlier task with 'Approve' and 'Approve with comments'; after approving, the run showed 'Workflow run completed'. Reports showed the open run under Active Workflow Runs (2 of 7 tasks, on track) and the finished one under Recently Completed. The sample 'Start Here' workflow also counts as a run.

The CSV export from Reports has 13 run-level columns even with 'Export all columns', with times in UTC, but none of the form values we entered (purchase ID, amounts 10 and 20). Active and completed runs are separate exports.

The trial bar said '14 days left in your free trial' on the day of sign-up, and no card was asked. The organisation name we entered during onboarding was not used: the workspace was named after the account holder instead.
On the first attempt the 'Workflow Name' field stayed empty after the AI filled in the rest; typing the name worked.
not_tested: Multiple users and a real role split
sessions.note: Findings as written up after the session; no pass/fail per task was scored.

open_questions.question: Can you publish a price, or a starting price, for the plans that are quote-only?
Can a customer cancel at any time, and what happens to an annual plan that is cancelled mid-term?
Which data can a customer export, in which formats, on which plans?
Where is customer data stored, and can a customer choose the region?
Is there a minimum number of seats or users on any plan?
